brief: A box-score specimen wall in committed jade, fat carnival slab small-caps, the lit field winning 144-140.
rationale:
The phrase came first: the Pistons won a shootout 144-140, both teams past 140, and the only line that is both quotable and unmistakably Doug's is the dry observation that nobody played any defense. That decides the object: the page is the offense, a crowded masonry wall of the night's numbers, with the wry statement woven in as the dominant tile rather than a lone centered hero. The near-even score decides the symmetry: evenly-packed columns, matched weight on both sides, with a dark forest field and a lit jade field trading points so the value split, not the layout, carries the win.

The chassis is alfa-rubik because a 284-point track meet wants a fat, physical, carnival-loud slab, not another condensed signage face or editorial serif, and Alfa Slab One has gone unused while three condensed faces and the serifs have carried recent nights. Its single weight and lack of italics forces an honest regular/roman treatment, so the variance lives in small-caps, justified, and type-as-texture instead: the 144 and 140 set as oversized specimen numerals are the wall's material. The palette is committed single-hue jade (158°, dead inside the mandate) because the brightness itself reads as scoreboard heat, and one electric accent green closes the score line without needing a second hue.

Layout follows: a four-column masonry on hairline gutters, the hero tile spanning the top-left two columns and two rows, the header folded into the top row with a horizontal lockup on the dark forest field where the white disc of the mark clears contrast easily. Split-field is the ground strategy because the two color fields are the composition, and it is off the recently-overused drench/duotone/light-ground formulas. At 360 the wall stacks, leading with the statement tile, then the 144/140 pair as adjacent full-width bands so the shootout survives the collapse.

hero.rationale:
The Pistons won a track meet last night, both teams past 140, and a Detroit box score is the one signal this morning that is unambiguously Doug's. The Jefferson quote is well made but it is about anger, not design, engineering, golf, Detroit or the work, so it fails the "would Doug say this" test and loses to a wry line about the score. A composed line beats a bare "144-140" because the joke is the point: when a game ends 144-140, the defense took the night off. This is the same lane as yesterday, justified because the shootout is the only live, owned, Doug-register signal in the set and a flat score wouldn't carry a hero.
Owner's voice: A score is a score, and Doug would laugh that two NBA teams scored 284 points between them and call it exactly what it was.

adBrief.selfCheck:
1. Hero quotability: Yes — "Nobody guarded anybody, 144-140" is a complete wry take you could screenshot, not a label.
2. Because-of chain: Yes — shootout line → packed symmetric specimen wall → fat carnival slab (alfa-rubik) → committed electric jade → interleaved hero tile.
3. Render feasibility: Yes — hero clamps to ~148px under alfa-rubik's 160px ceiling, justified small-caps fills the two-column tile without overflow.
4. Canvas floor feasible: Yes — a crowded masonry of colored tiles fills well past 82% of 1440×900.
5. Phone: Yes — collapse stack leads with the hero tile at `3xl`, which fits "anybody" inside 360 without cutting a word.

adBrief.compositionRationale: The phrase is a wry one-liner about a night of pure offense, so the page is the offense: a crowded, evenly-gutted masonry wall of the night's numbers with the statement woven in as the dominant tile. I moved hero_zone off the starting `center` to `interleaved` because a masonry wants its hero as a tile among tiles, not floating with clearance, and hero_object off `word` to `statement` because the quotable line, not a single word, is the largest object. Symmetric packing is kept deliberately: 144-140 was a near-even game, so even columns and matched weight on both sides are the structure, with the value split (dark field vs lit jade) carrying the result instead of layout imbalance.

colorScheme.color_story: Electric jade lit against deep forest, a bright field and a dark one trading points, the lit side winning 144-140.

shell.footer: split colophon band — the day's facts in a final full-width band split across the two field greens, no reversal beyond the fields

header.nav: folded into the hero's top row — horizontal lockup (mark + "Doug March", role beneath) at top-left on the deep forest field where the white disc carries easily; 01 02 03 work / about / contact as numbered specimen links at top-right. Mark inside the first fold at 1440 and 360.

verdicts.feedback:
1. (Judgment 5) The role line under the wordmark reads "DESIGN & ENGINEERING" on desktop and on the phone, and the colophon repeats it as "ROLE Design & Engineering". The record's role is "Product Designer & Developer"; use that string in both places.
2. (Judgment 5) The colophon rows "FOCUS Design that is the product" and "NOW FishSticks • 15th Club" don't match `personal.currentFocus`, which is "Building Spaceman and using AI as a force multiplier in product work". "BASED Aldie, Virginia" comes from the weather signal and is not in the records. Drop these rows or replace them with record text.
3. (Judgment 3) The Type Treatment says `alignment: justified`, but the hero is ragged-left at 1440. NOBODY / GUARDED / ANYBODY, / 144-140. end at four different widths, and "anybody," sits short at 360. Make the statement's lines fill the tile measure to a shared right edge, for example by tracking or sizing each line to the tile width.
4. (Judgment 6) The Mobile Declaration's `nav_360` says the role line drops at 360, but fold 1 still shows "DESIGN & ENGINEERING" under "Doug March". Hide it at the phone width.

1. Hierarchy (Type Treatment `alignment: justified`): at 1440 the hero is set one word per line and left-aligned with ragged edges ("NOBODY" is far shorter than "ANYBODY,"), so nothing reads as justified. Re-break the statement into full-measure lines that justify edge to edge across the tile, for example "Nobody guarded / anybody, 144-140.", or space the letters so each line fills the measure.
2. Hierarchy and legibility at 360: in fold 1 the score breaks across lines as "144-" / "140.". It reads as a hyphenated word, and the joke's punchline is broken in two. Keep "144-140." together with a non-breaking hyphen or `white-space: nowrap` so it sits whole on its own line.
3. Copy (judgment 5): in fold 4 the dougmar.ch tile is labelled "FEATURED · AI · 2026". The work records mark Spaceman as the featured project (`featured: true`), and dougmar.ch is not featured. Drop "Featured" from dougmar.ch, or lead the work index with Spaceman as the featured project.

The mockup does what the brief declared: the slab small-caps statement is the dominant tile of a crowded jade-and-forest masonry wall. At 1440 the full statement sits inside the first fold, and the lit 144 tile against the dark 140 tile tells the score through the light/dark split rather than the layout. At 360 the statement leads fold 1, followed by the 144/140 pair and the rest in the declared order, ending on the split colophon band.

measurables.method: Measured at 1440x900 on a 20px grid over the viewport at scroll position zero. canvas_utilization: % of grid cells touched by an element carrying designed content (visible text, an image/SVG/video/canvas, a background colour distinct from the page background and not transparent, or a background image such as a gradient). A background set on html or body counts as painting the page, unless it is opaque white; ::before and ::after boxes count on the same terms. color_coverage: % of grid cells whose sampled background, background-image stops or text colour is chromatic (HSL saturation > 12%, lightness 8-92%). hero_px: the largest computed font-size among first-fold elements that set visible text.
